https://www.jacarandafm.com/news/news/ms.text: Evidence led at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry shed light on an alleged deal involving sophisticated surveillance equipment. Anastasi Mokgobu/Jacaranda FM News Chief evidence leader Matthew Chaskalson presented WhatsApp messages from the phone of late taxi boss Jothan Msibi, concerning a Czech company that was looking to sell devices known as “catchers”. He explained that the technology can mimic cellphone towers and intercept data from mobile devices. The messages involved Msibi, Katiso “KT” Molefe and suspended Sergeant Fannie Nkosi. A man who identified himself as “Shane”, but was saved in Nkosi’s phone as Shaun Jacobs, contacted the officer about documentation needed for the Czech company to demonstrate its equipment to the South African Police Service. Jacobs sent Nkosi a document and asked him to place it on South African Police Service (SAPS) letterhead or that of an official police unit. Nkosi allegedly signed the document using his force number and a SAPS stamp. The document was then sent to Msibi. Chaskalson told the commission that Msibi subsequently used it in dealings with Molefe and Steve Motsumi as they sought potential buyers for the surveillance equipment in Eswatini. “So, Sergeant Nkosi has represented to the Czech government that the company will be presenting to the SAPS and should be allowed to do so,” said the evidence leader. R1.6 MILLION EQUIPMENT DEAL Chaskalson also presented a flight itinerary showing that Motsumi and Msibi had booked a trip to Europe in connection with the procurement of tactical equipment worth R1.6 million. The equipment was intended for Themy Styles, a company in which Msibi and Molefe were listed as owner and director respectively. “Mr Msibi, Mr Motsumi, Mr Molefe and possibly Sergeant Nkosi were involved in a commercial project which involves the selling of high-tech surveillance systems and jamming technology,” said Chaskalson. ESWATINI DEAL STALLS The proposed sale of the surveillance equipment to Eswatini, however, appears to have stalled. Messages showed Jacobs and Nkosi attempting to finalise a contract between the Czech suppliers and the prospective Swazi buyers. But the process was delayed after Nkosi stopped responding to Jacobs for several weeks. One of Msibi’s messages to Nkosi appeared to express frustration over the delays while also referring to further potential government business. “You know there’s so much work we wanted to do with you. We have many solutions that are in demand by government, but we wanted to do this deal first before we can introduce other solutions,” one of Msibi’s last messages to Nkosi read. Commissioner Advocate Sandile Khumalo questioned Chaskalson about the inference he was drawing from the evidence. Chaskalson suggested the evidence pointed to an alleged fraudulent scheme involving those who were aware of the circumstances surrounding Nkosi’s letter. “The inference is that it’s an out-and-out fraud, but it’s a fraud to which everyone involved in that project is party – everyone involved in that project with knowledge of Sergeant Nkosi’s letter." https://www.westmeathindependent.ie/2026.text: Published: Fri 16 Oct 2026, 6:23 PM MEP Ciaran Mullooly. Just Transition 'failing to create enough jobs in Midlands': MEP Published: Fri 16 Oct 2026, 6:23 PM The level of investment and job creation in the Midlands through the EU Just Transition programme is falling far short of the level required to sustain communities in the region impacted by the loss of peat production, MEP Ciaran Mullooly has warned. A report this week by Indecon found there were issues with "the long-term sustainable impact" of the Just Transition fund. It said projects supported by the EU fund had been expected to create up to 1,094 full or part-time jobs, but that just 183 posts had actually been created. Commenting on this report, MEP Mullooly said he was "disappointed but not surprised" by the findings, which also showed that just €16 million of the €22.2 million allocated to the fund had been drawn down. Government analysis found that more than 1,000 employees and contractors were directly impacted by the transition away from peat production in the Midlands. "This report confirms what I have been saying from day one: announcing proposals and funding is not the same as delivering investment and replacement livelihoods for the people affected," Mr Mullooly said. "The investment and employment our communities were led to expect have not materialised on the scale required. "More alarmingly, I do not believe they will materialise unless the policy changes. The approach is wrong because it is not sufficiently focused on the people and places that lost their livelihoods." Mr Mullooly said the fund should have been built around practical routes into work and stronger support for local employers. "My position has been clear: we needed a skills-based approach, a dedicated apprenticeship scheme and much stronger support for small and medium-sized businesses willing to invest and employ locally. "But the application process was weighed down by red tape, while State aid rules also affected applications." He said the economic consequences of ending peat harvesting and closing power stations in the Midlands reached far beyond the plants themselves. "The ending of peat harvesting by Bord na Móna, the closure of the power stations and the impact on associated businesses struck at the heart of the Midlands economy. "These were political choices with consequences for workers, contractors, families and entire communities. "Peat extraction continues in other European countries, including Latvia and Estonia. People in the Midlands are entitled to ask why their industry was shut down before adequate replacement employment was in place," he added. "People in the Midlands were given barely a year to prepare. A previous government Just Transition Progress Report stated that a transition expected to take ten years had been reduced to twelve months, possibly shorter. "Compare that with Poland, where the agreed coal-mine phase-out timetable runs to the end of 2049 and five regions there have been allocated €3.85 billion from the EU Just Transition Fund for 2021–27. "Our communities deserved the same kind of long-term planning and serious investment," the Independent Ireland representative concluded. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/26/292-.text: When Oliver Schäfer feels what is on the other end of his line, he quickly realises that this is no ordinary fish. The 34-year-old, from the western German state of North Rhine-Westphalia, is taking part in a predator fishing tournament in the southern Polish city of Rybnik in Poland, together with his Dutch fishing partner Kevin Cremers.On 10 and 11 October, 70 teams with around 150 anglers from all over Europe competed there, according to the German newspaper Bild. Schäfer and Cremers had travelled specifically for the event. As Schäfer told the newspaper, the pair were fishing with a special rod designed for large catfish and a soft plastic lure.Schafer only grasped how enormous his adversary was when the fish broke the surface for the first time. The fight lasted more than 30 minutes. Cremers kept the boat on course against the wind, while Schäfer held.Measured and released againBack on shore, judges measured the catfish at 292 centimetres. It was then returned to the lake, as tournament rules require. Schäfer told Bild that the fish are brought ashore on a tarpaulin so that their protective mucus slime layer is not damaged.However, the catch alone was not enough to win the tournament, which was decided on total points. According to the Berliner Zeitung and the results list of the anglers’ association PZW Katowice published by the Katowice branch of the Polish Angling Association (PZW), the duo finished second with 28,930 points.There are, of course, other impressive specimens in the lake as well. On Instagram, Schäfer reports that he and Cremers targeted zander at sunrise. Their catches, including a fish measuring 81 centimetres, earned them "a good number of points" for the overall standings.Is it the same fish caught last year?The catfish has a backstory. According to media reports, participants believe it is the same fish that was caught during the tournament in October 2025. On that occasion, Polish anglers Krzysztof Pyra and Adrian Gontarz landed a catfish that also measured 292 centimetres. The Berliner Zeitung reports that the fish has not grown any longer since, but has become noticeably more bulkier.International Game Fish Association (IGFA), the sport’s global governing body, keeps catfish records by weight, and there is no official list based on length. According to the German daily Welt Die Welt, Italian angler Alessandro Biancardi landed a catfish measuring 2.85 metres from the River Po in 2023.The Polish city of Rybnik in the Silesian Voivodeship is therefore regarded, especially among anglers, as the place where the longest known catfish has been caught.Schäfer’s dream of a three-metre catfish remains alive even after this angling success. He told BILD he was now "just a hand’s breadth" away.Europe’s largest freshwater fishAccording to Germany’s Federal Agency for Nature Conservation, the European catfish is the continent’s largest native freshwater fish. It can grow up to three metres long and weigh as much as 150 kilograms. Striking features include its scaleless body, broad head and six barbels that help it find its way in murky water.It feeds mainly on fish; larger individuals occasionally prey on small waterbirds or mammals. For 2026, the anglers’ association, the Federal Agency for Nature Conservation and the Ichthyological Society have chosen the catfish as fish of the year.Thriving in warmer watersOriginally, the catfish was native mainly to the Danube and Rhine river systems. Stocking programmes dating back to the 19th century and waterways such as the Main-Danube Canal have since opened up many more habitats to the species, according to the agency.Climate change is also helping. As a warmth-loving species, catfish benefit from rising water temperatures. Biologist Jürgen Geist told the German news magazine Focus that populations are increasing markedly, both in range and in density. By contrast, cold-water species such as the brown trout are among the losers.Warmth also plays a role in Rybnik. The reservoir serves as a cooling basin for a coal-fired power plant, and the heated water is discharged back into it. Because fish feed more actively at higher temperatures, catfish, carp and zander grow faster there, according to Schäfer.Experts say the fish pose little danger to humans. They have only small rasping teeth, and outside the spawning season there is virtually no risk. However, in June 2025, a catfish measuring around two metres in length bit several swimmers in Brombachsee in Middle Franconia, causing minor injuries.

https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/ince.text: Cel puțin patru persoane au murit și alte 35 au fost rănite în urma unui incendiu izbucnit sâmbătă la o centrală electrică din sudul Irakului. Flăcările s-au extins și la locuințele din apropiere, iar activitatea centralei a fost oprită, potrivit oficialilor din domeniul securității. Incendiul a izbucnit la centrala electrică Hartha, situată la nord de orașul Basra. Echipele de protecție civilă au intervenit și au reușit să aducă flăcările sub control, potrivit agenției de presă irakiene INA. Potrivit celulei de presă pentru securitate din Irak, incendiul a izbucnit în jurul orei locale 6:00. Cele mai multe victime au fost înregistrate în rândul locuitorilor caselor afectate de flăcări, care au suferit arsuri și intoxicații cu fum. Ministerul irakian al Electricității a transmis că incidentul a implicat o conductă de gaz care alimenta centrala. Cu toate acestea, cauza exactă a incendiului nu a fost stabilită oficial. În urma incidentului, centrala și-a întrerupt activitatea. Unitatea are o capacitate instalată de 800 de megawați, însă înainte de izbucnirea incendiului funcționa la aproximativ 400 de megawați. Premierul irakian a cerut deschiderea unei anchete urgente pentru stabilirea cauzelor incidentului și identificarea responsabilităților. Autoritățile nu au comunicat deocamdată amploarea pagubelor produse de incendiu. Urmărește știrile Digi24.ro și pe Google News

https://www.portfolio.hu/gazdasag/202611.text: A tárca már megkezdte az országos bejelentővédelmi és szervezeti kultúrafejlesztési program kidolgozását. A kezdeményezés az egészségügy valamennyi dolgozójára kiterjedne , az orvosoktól és ápolóktól kezdve a szakdolgozókon át az intézmények többi munkatársáig. A tervezett rendszerben korrupciót, összeférhetetlenséget, etikátlan szakmai gyakorlatot, megfélemlítést, kizsákmányolást és mérgező munkahelyi légkört is jelezni lehetne. Külön figyelmet fordítanának azokra az esetekre, amikor valakit egy korábbi munkahelyéről próbálnak szakmailag ellehetetleníteni. A LÉPÉS Program öt szakmai pillérre épülne. Ezek közé tartozik a helyi szervezeti tanulás és a jó gyakorlatok terjesztése, a bejelentők érdemi védelme, a hatóságok kezdeményező felügyelete, a méltányos felelősségmegállapítás és a szabad megszólalás biztosítása. A minisztérium bizalmas és névtelen bejelentési lehetőségeket, képzett helyi bizalmi személyekből álló hálózatot, valamint az intézményi vezetéstől független bejelentési utakat alakítana ki. A rendszer nemcsak a visszaélések feltárását szolgálná, hanem a dolgozók fejlesztési javaslatainak összegyűjtését és a jól működő intézményi megoldások elterjesztését is. A program fontos eleme lenne annak megkülönböztetése, hogy egy adott probléma nem szándékos emberi hibából, rendszerszintű hiányosságból vagy tudatos visszaélésből ered-e. A cél az arányos felelősségmegállapítás, miközben a korrupció, a szándékos veszélyeztetés és a megtorlás továbbra is következményekkel járna. Az egyik legjelentősebb tervezett változás az lenne, hogy a hatóságoknak nem kellene minden esetben hivatalos bejelentésre várniuk. Ha egy újságcikk, televíziós riport, közösségi médiás bejegyzés vagy más nyilvános dokumentum konkrét, ellenőrizhető tényeket, illetve súlyos visszaélés megalapozott gyanúját tárja fel, az illetékes szerveknek értékelniük kellene az információkat, és indokolt esetben hivatalból vizsgálatot indítaniuk. A hivatalos bejelentés hiánya sem lehet indok arra, hogy egy súlyos, ellenőrizhető problémával ne foglalkozzunk A miniszter hangsúlyozta, hogy egy sajtóban vagy közösségi médiában megjelent állítás önmagában nem bizonyít jogsértést, ezért az érintetteket nem lehet előzetesen elítélni. Ugyanakkor a visszaélések feltárásával járó kockázatokat sem lehet kizárólag a kiszolgáltatott helyzetben lévő dolgozókra hárítani. A LÉPÉS Program kidolgozásakor több nemzetközi modellt is figyelembe vennének. Az angol egészségügyi szolgálat, az NHS Freedom to Speak Up rendszeréből a biztonságos megszólalás lehetőségét és a helyi bizalmi személyek hálózatát vennék át. A 2015 után fokozatosan kiépített rendszerben a 2025/2026-os időszakban már közel 38 ezer ügyet jeleztek. A dán betegbiztonsági rendszerből a hibák okainak feltárását és a hasonló esetek megelőzését, a skót gyakorlatból a bejelentések független felülvizsgálatát, az írből pedig a bizalmas adatkezelést és a bejelentők támogatását hasznosítanák. Az ausztrál modell a hivatalból induló vizsgálatokhoz és a példaértékű munkahelyi magatartás elismeréséhez szolgálna mintaként. A nemzetközi tapasztalatok alapján a szervezeti kultúra átalakítása hosszú folyamat lehet. Angliában több mint tíz, Dániában több mint húsz éve fejlesztik a kapcsolódó rendszereket, Skóciában pedig közel hat év telt el a független bejelentővédelmi rendszer tervének bejelentésétől annak teljes elindításáig. Egy 2024-ben publikált, öt ausztrál kórházra kiterjedő vizsgálat ugyanakkor már két és fél–három év után mérhető javulást mutatott a tiszteletlen és zaklató munkahelyi magatartások visszaszorításában. A minisztérium a már elindított betegvisszajelző rendszer mellett az egészségügyi dolgozók tapasztalatait is beépítené az ágazat fejlesztésébe. A tervezett program megvalósításában a hatóságokra, a fenntartókra, a kórházi vezetőkre, a szakmai kamarákra és az érdekképviseletekre is feladat hárulna. A miniszter szerint önmagában egy új informatikai felület, jogszabály vagy miniszteri utasítás nem elegendő a változáshoz. Ehhez az intézményi vezetési gyakorlat és a munkahelyi viszonyok átalakítására is szükség lenne. A hibáztatás és a félelem kultúrájából a méltányosságon és az igazságos felelősségvállaláson keresztül a tanulás és a folyamatos fejlődés kultúrájába kell eljutnunk A tárca egyelőre a program kidolgozásán dolgozik, annak bevezetési időpontját nem közölték. Photograph: CPS/PA View image in fullscreen Alexander Lewis-Ranwell being released from a police station. Photograph: CPS/PA Police Man who killed three during psychotic episode ‘had been released after catalogue of failures’ Alexander Lewis-Ranwell was arrested and let go twice by police in the 48 hours before he killed three men in their 80s in Exeter Rachel Hall Sun 22 Nov 2026 08.24 EST Last modified on Sun 22 Nov 2026 08.26 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A man with paranoid schizophrenia who killed three people while experiencing a psychotic episode had been released from custody after a “catalogue of failures” by police and medical professionals, an investigation has found. Alexander Lewis-Ranwell was arrested and released twice by police in the 48 hours before he killed Anthony Payne, 80, and the twin brothers Roger and Dick Carter, 84, in their homes in Exeter in 2019. Officers were found to have ignored warnings from a national database as well as a mental health assessor, according to a joint investigation by the Sunday Times and BBC Radio 4’s File On 4 Investigates. Numerous failings were found in hours of police video, detention logs and witness testimony. The medical professional who was sent to examine Lewis-Ranwell, 27, did not have expertise in mental health and dismissed his unpredictable behaviour. There were also failures to record and share key details that would have built up a picture of the severity of Lewis-Ranwell’s mental illness. Officers did not know that by law they had the power to detain him under the Mental Health Act without a medical assessment. Warnings from Lewis-Ranwell’s mother, that he was having a psychotic episode and should be kept in custody, were also ignored. View image in fullscreen Alexander Lewis-Ranwell. Photograph: Devon and Cornwall police/PA The families of the three men have called on the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) to open an investigation into Devon and Cornwall police, but they are still waiting for answers and an apology. The watchdog has said that the force should investigate itself, but they have heard nothing for two years. Two days before the murders took place, Lewis-Ranwell was arrested after breaking into a farm. After his release he was arrested a second time for attacking a farmer with a 1.2-metre (4ft) logging saw. Despite exhibiting disturbing behaviour in custody – police bodycam footage shows him semi-naked, hissing, spitting and punching at the hatch window to his cell, while ranting about paedophiles and seeing animals – he was released again. Following a rampage that lasted hours and in which he threatened multiple people, he killed the three men, bludgeoning Payne with a hammer and killing the twins with a spade. A trial at Exeter crown court in December 2019 found Lewis-Ranwell not guilty by reason of insanity. He was given a hospital restriction order, where he will stay until agencies are confident he could be released back into the community. One psychiatrist who studied the case told the court he believed Lewis-Ranwell, a former public schoolboy from Croyde, north Devon , was “one of the illest people” he had come across. Last month an inquest found failings by police led to his release after a doctor missed “clear signs of delusion and disordered thinking”. Amanda Taylor told the Sunday Times that her family was still seeking justice for her uncles the Carter brothers and that they want the IOPC to revisit the case. “All I want is for just one of the agencies involved to stand up and say: ‘We are so sorry. Serious mistakes were made. We recognise the devastating consequences of those failures and we will do everything in our power to make sure this never happens again,’” she said. Lewis-Ranwell’s case is one of several where failures from the police and mental health services to manage risk have resulted in tragedy. A review by the Care Quality Commission of the treatment of Valdo Calocane, who has paranoid schizophrenia and killed three people in Nottingham in 2023, concluded that a “series of errors and misjudgments” led to him being discharged, despite repeatedly not taking medication and showing signs of aggression. The report concluded that there are “systemic issues with community mental health care which, without immediate action, will continue to pose an inherent risk to patient and public safety”. NHS England has since strengthened guidance around community mental health support for people with severe mental illnesses who face high risk or struggle to engage with services. Noting that there are an estimated 100 to 120 mental health-related killings in the UK every year, Julian Hendy, of the victims’ charity Hundred Families, said: “In my view, had the lessons in the Lewis-Ranwell case been learnt earlier, and effective action taken, there is a real chance that the Nottingham attacks could well have been prevented. Services aren’t learning and totally innocent people are losing their lives as a result.” A police spokesperson said the force was addressing “areas of learning” and would reflect on the recommendations of the inquest jury, adding: “Our thoughts, as always, remain with the loved ones of Anthony Payne and Dick and Roger Carter.” The IOPC said the family had a right to ask for a review of the internal investigation and that it had not yet received a request.
